source.title: Using physics-inspired Singular Learning Theory to understand grokking & other phase transitions in modern neural networks

record.tranche_reason: The study trains networks on modular addition and measures grokking transition times and free-energy changes, using an SLT-based analysis rather than testing the full original accuracy-versus-training-set-size claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that 168 of 500 modular-arithmetic runs grokked and plots transition-time results. It does not report a training-set-size sweep. Its Toy Models of Superposition experiment concerns aesthetic phase transitions that the paper explicitly contrasts with grokking. The remaining LLC scaling experiments do not test the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses modular addition only as a setting known to grok, to test its own Arrhenius-style free-energy/transition-time hypothesis. The 168/500 grokking count is a selection filter for that analysis. It reports no accuracy trajectories, no delay magnitudes and no training-set-size variation, so its results do not bear on whether V1 or any other version holds. The reader's T2/tests guess is too generous.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors report mixed evidence for the Arrhenius-style relation: a negative slope with low R2 on modular addition, and inconclusive, detection-sensitive results on Toy Models of Superposition. They also report LLC scaling results (Question 2) that are unrelated to grokking.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the modular-addition grokking setup, but focuses on SLT free energy and LLC rather than directly reporting accuracy trajectories or comparing grokking delays across training-set sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: For the Toy Models of Superposition experiment, the inferred free-energy/time slope varied with the transition-detection method; the authors report recovering a downward slope with a more rudimentary, non-smoothing approach.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 168 grokking modular-addition runs (p=53, 40% train), the change in SLT free energy from memorization to grokking shows a negative slope against log time-to-grok, with low R2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The time from memorization to grokking scales exponentially with the free-energy drop (an Arrhenius-style rate).

fits_no_version.finding: On Toy Models of Superposition phase transitions, the free-energy/time fit slope reverses depending on the transition-detection method; the authors deem this inconclusive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The Arrhenius-style free-energy/time relation extends to non-grokking phase transitions.

record.problems: For the claim-relevant experiment, only 168 of 500 runs are analyzed as grokking runs; the paper does not provide numerical transition-time values in the text or vary training-set size. The reported relationship has low R2. The separate Toy Models of Superposition result is described as highly sensitive to transition-detection method and inconclusive.
record.rows_left_out: The LLC-jump distribution in Figure 2 and the Toy Models of Superposition transition analysis in Figure 4 were not included as claim-version rows: they do not measure the circuit formation or delayed generalization named by the versions. Question 2 LLC-scaling results are also outside the listed versions.

untested.parts: Whether test accuracy jumps from chance to near-perfect after training saturation (no curves or numbers given), and whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks (only a 40% split is used).
Circuit formation, removal of memorizing components, and whether progress measures anticipate the jump. LLC is measured only before and after the grok, not as a predictor of it.

record.verdict_notes: Training hyperparameters (epochs, weight decay, optimizer) are not given, so the 33.6% grokking rate cannot be read as evidence on how reliably grokking occurs. The study cites Power et al. 2022, an original source, only as the setup. The Question 2 LLC-scaling experiments do not bear on any version.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses only p=53 with a 40% training subset; it does not vary training-set size or report whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks. It does not provide numerical training/test-accuracy trajectories or a numerical delay.

It measures LLC around grokking, but does not identify a generalizing circuit, track Fourier-algorithm formation, measure removal of memorizing components, or show that a continuous circuit-progress measure anticipates the accuracy jump.
The non-algorithmic Toy Models of Superposition experiment studies aesthetic phase transitions, not delayed generalization; it does not vary initialization scale or weight norm.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is studied.
The study does not test whether weight decay or low norm favors a more efficient generalizing circuit, nor a critical dataset size or ungrokking.
It does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
It does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point limits as explanations for grokking.

rows.subject: modulo-arithmetic toy networks (p=53; aggregate of 500 runs)
rows.operation_detail: Counted runs in which grokking occurred

conditions.value: randomly chosen 40% subset of Z53 × Z53

rows.note: The paper defines memorization as 100% training accuracy with poor test accuracy and grokking as 100% training and test accuracy. The count is an aggregate across 500 runs.
rows.check: This is a selection value: the authors 'only considered the 168 (33.6%) runs' that grokked, for their free-energy analysis. Training length, weight decay and optimizer are not stated, and the non-grokking runs are not characterised. The count cannot show V1's chance-to-perfect jump or its dependence on dataset size, and the reader's 'partial' state has no basis against V1.

source_check.correct: 168 of 500 runs (33.6%) were selected for subsequent analysis because grokking occurred. Retain as selection metadata rather than a claim-testing result row.
source_check.problem: The count is accurate, but verdict_rules.md excludes selection values from result rows.

rows.measure: log(r_i→j), where r_i→j = j−i is the time from memorization to grokking
rows.note: The paper reports a histogram of log transition times but gives no numerical values or textual characterization of their magnitudes.
rows.check: The transition time is defined between a memorized checkpoint and a grokked checkpoint, so a delay exists by construction. The histogram is figure-only, with no values. It is used as the input variable for the Arrhenius test, not as a measurement of V1.

relation.reason: The study analyzes selected grokking runs to test an Arrhenius-style relationship, rather than testing a listed claim version.

tranche.reason: Uses grokking as the experimental setting for its own free-energy/transition-time hypothesis. The reported analyses do not establish the accuracy-jump shape, delay magnitude, dataset-size dependence, or mechanisms specified by the claim versions.

source_check.notes: Training duration, training optimizer and weight decay are unstated; Appendix SGLD settings concern LLC estimation. Time-based metrics were recorded at 100 linearly spaced checkpoints.
